system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer-side review

*This review is based only on the Seller update and disclosure letter; the full SPA and underlying DD documents may reveal additional issues.*

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A cap of **100% of the AUD 24m price**, with at least **50%** as a commercial fallback; separate higher or uncapped regimes for title, tax, indemnities, fraud and covenants. | **Reject 20% and open at 100% (fallback 50%)** — AUD 4.8m is inadequate protection for a whole-business acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 **deductible** basket, so only excess is recoverable. | No thresholds ideally; otherwise a lower de minimis, a **tipping basket**, aggregation of related claims and no thresholds for fundamental, tax, indemnity, covenant or fraud claims. | **Counter with AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket** — the proposed thresholds suppress legitimate claims and leave Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General claims must be notified within **18 months**; Seller seeks limitations across all claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24–36 months** for general warranties, with notification preserving a claim until finally resolved and separate periods for other categories. | **Require 24 months minimum and express category-specific periods** — 18 months may expire before latent issues emerge through a full audit cycle. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same **20% cap, thresholds and 18-month limit** as general warranties. | **100% purchase-price cap**, no de minimis or basket, and at least seven years—or no contractual time limit—for title, capacity and authority claims. | **Reject the general-warranty regime for fundamental/title claims** — Buyer must receive and retain valid title to what it is paying AUD 24m to acquire. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | No express carve-out is identified; Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to **all Claims of any nature**. | Express disapplication of every cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy, knowledge and non-reliance provision for fraud, fraudulent concealment and deliberate or wilful misconduct. | **Insert a comprehensive fraud/deliberate-concealment carve-out** — Seller must not contractually benefit from dishonest withholding or misrepresentation. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records, without admitting materiality or legal effect. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature, scope and likely consequences, against identified warranties; no general public-record or data-room dump. | **Delete general disclosure and require warranty-specific fair disclosure** — Buyer should not have to reconstruct exceptions from an undifferentiated document repository. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything Buyer or its advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records. | No knowledge qualifier; fallback limited to **actual, conscious knowledge of named senior Buyer personnel**, excluding advisers, constructive knowledge and any duty to investigate. | **Delete clause 8.3 or confine it to named persons’ actual knowledge** — the proposed wording converts due diligence access into a broad release of Seller liability. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of counterparty’s written consent, although no final consent or evidence of satisfying clause 11.3 conditions exists. | A genuine condition precedent requiring **unconditional and effective consent**, satisfaction of all related conditions, no adverse amendment or payment, and Buyer approval of its form. | **Do not complete until Bluefen consent and all conditions are verified** — Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue and cannot be left to endeavours or deemed satisfaction. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; release is proposed **after Completion**. | Repayment and irrevocable discharge of all security **at or before Completion**, supported by a payoff letter, direct funds-flow payment and release documents held in escrow. | **Make repayment and release simultaneous completion deliverables** — Buyer must not acquire shares subject to Seller-era debt or security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are Seller’s matter and omitted from funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unidentified. | Seller to pay and bear all bonuses and on-costs, or have the full amount treated as debt/leakage and deducted from price, with an indemnity for any Company liability. | **Add the grossed-up liability to completion adjustments or require pre-funding** — the bonuses are triggered by the sale and should not reduce the debt-free/cash-free value delivered to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 remains open and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is available. | Pre-Completion cleared payment, evidence of vesting/assignment, and a specific indemnity covering all loss from non-payment, defective ownership, non-transfer or third-party IP claims. | **Expand the indemnity and require title evidence before Completion** — paying AUD 180,000 alone does not establish that critical IP has validly transferred. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Treated as preliminary and not expected to be material; possible export of about 1,240 records, with access, scope and notification obligations unresolved. | Full investigation before Completion, preservation and remediation steps, regulatory/privacy advice, notification compliance, continuing cooperation and a specific indemnity not subject to general thresholds or cap. | **Require a remediation covenant plus specific indemnity, with escrow if exposure remains open** — an unresolved privacy incident can create post-Completion regulatory, customer and remediation costs. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000 total) characterised as ordinary-course operating costs, despite uncertainty about timing, termination and accrual. | Full contracts and invoices, confirmation of commitment and termination rights, no renewal or variation without Buyer consent, and appropriate working-capital/debt-like treatment for pre-Completion liabilities. | **Reserve price treatment until the obligations are verified** — “ordinary course” does not determine whether AUD 330,000 is accrued, avoidable or properly borne by Seller. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller seeks caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions applying to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Separate regimes for general warranties, title/fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, leakage/debt adjustments, completion obligations and fraud/statutory claims. | **Rewrite the limitations schedule by claim category** — a single general regime would improperly dilute specifically negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the Company’s DD-012 share register as evidence that Seller owns 100% of the shares. | Share certificates, executed transfers, updated register, ASIC and PPSR searches, evidence of no options or third-party rights, releases of security and robust title/capitalisation warranties. | **Make independent title and encumbrance verification a Completion requirement** — a company-maintained register alone does not prove unencumbered ownership or exclude competing rights. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP are “settled” under the **20%/18-month general warranty regime**. | Tax indemnity plus comprehensive tax warranties, normally surviving to the statutory assessment period plus a buffer and capped at 100%; robust IP ownership, validity, infringement, open-source and employee/contractor assignment protections with longer or specific recovery. | **Keep tax and IP expressly open and outside the general regime** — both can generate substantial latent liabilities well after 18 months and materially affect enterprise value. |

### Priority completion blockers

Buyer should treat the following as non-negotiable before Completion:

1. **Effective Bluefen consent**, including satisfaction of all associated conditions.
2. **Riverlark repayment and full security discharge at Completion.**
3. **Confirmed ownership/transfer of the Ironquay IP.**
4. **Full price treatment for bonuses and related on-costs.**
5. **Independent title and encumbrance verification.**
6. **A defined remediation and indemnity package for the export/privacy incident.**
=== END ADVICE ===
